title: `CORR`: three separate states; NaN for one pair or zero variance
verdict: cov / (std_x · std_y); NaN where the reference is NULL; no clamp
description: `CORR` keeps three independent states, a covariance and two Welford variances, and returns `cov / (std_x * std_y)`, NaN when `std_x * std_y == 0`. One pair or a zero variance gives NaN; no pairs gives NULL. Not clamped to [-1, 1]: with the separate states, |corr| can exceed 1 by a few ulps, more so than with a shared state. The square roots are taken separately, so the product of the variances does not overflow or underflow.

Probed: of no pairs (rows with a NULL on either side skipped) it is NULL; of one pair, of a side whose values are all equal, or where a variance underflows to 0 or overflows to inf, it is NaN, as is any NaN or ±inf input. Where the reference is NULL with at least one pair, DuckDB's is NaN; elsewhere they differ only in rounding (#85).
reference: `AggFn.corr` (`corrOf`): NULL for fewer than two pairs, or for a side whose values are all equal; else the co-deviation sum by the square root of the product of the two squared-deviation sums. It is not clamped to [-1, 1]. Engines may differ in the last bits (#54) until #85 bounds the error.
Where the reference is NULL (one pair, a constant side), DuckDB gives NaN; `Dialect.covar` leaves the NULL cases to its caller.

The SQL lift (`semantics="duckdb"`, the lift profile's `corr_degenerate="NAN"`) writes DuckDB's `CORR` as the reference's with a count of pairs, NaN where it is NULL and the count is positive (#433). With `semantics="reference"` it is the reference's.
